priority.override_reason: Ranks 1, 3, 4, and 5 are closed by current direct-leaf, static-object, native-callback, and raytrace profiling evidence; rank 2 remains a separate PropertyStorage allocation-family investigation rather than a call-exit mechanism. Fresh profiles of rank 6 CDjs and rank 12 date-format-tofte independently expose the same ordinary non-direct bytecode completion boundary. A value-only exit is a general, lower-risk prerequisite to any larger generic-frame scheduler and will be retained only if both targets clear the frozen gate.

mechanism.summary: For a synchronous ordinary bytecode function call whose caller needs only its completion value, keep the completed VM local and return Result<Value, RuntimeError> instead of materializing FunctionBytecodeResult and moving its CallEnv, locals, local-upvalue vector, and sloppy-global metadata through the caller before immediately dropping them.
mechanism.generality: Admission is determined only by the call's semantic role: ordinary synchronous bytecode calls use the value-only exit unless they are derived constructor calls whose caller must inspect the completed frame to implement implicit this return. Generator, async, async-generator, direct-slot, direct-eval, module, and derived-constructor flows retain their existing entry and result behavior. It does not inspect source paths, workload names, function names, argument values, iteration counts, checksums, or benchmark identities.
semantic_risks: retaining the full FunctionBytecodeResult path for derived construction so super-bound this, implicit object return, and missing-super errors remain observable
preserving immutable function-name caller restoration after both successful and abrupt ordinary calls
preserving the existing full-frame result APIs for direct eval and other evaluators whose callers inspect environment or slot state
dropping the completed ordinary frame in the same order on return and throw so captured-cell identity, using disposal, sloppy-global state, and thrown-value identity do not change
not widening direct-leaf eligibility or altering generator, async, class-constructor, proxy, bound-function, or native-call dispatch
